entry.title: The symplectic leaves of the affine Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme associated with a singular subalgebroid
entry.summary: Every singular subalgebroid, and in particular every singular foliation $\mathscr{G}$, determines a universal Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$, which is the analogue of the linear Poisson structure on the dual of a Lie algebroid. We show that the underlying space $X_{\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G})}$ of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$ decomposes as a disjoint union of symplectic manifolds. Furthermore, we extend the Helffer-Nourrigat cone to a singular subalgebroid and show that it is an embedded Poisson $C^\infty$-subscheme of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$.

entry.title: Space curves in Hahn calculus: rotation structure, a fundamental theorem, and $q$-deformed invariants at the fixed point
entry.summary: We develop the differential geometry of space curves in Hahn's quantum calculus, where the derivative is the difference quotient along the contraction $σ(t)=qt+ω$ with fixed point $ω_0=ω/(1-q)$. The Hahn Frenet frame is transported along every orbit of $σ$ by rotations through turning and torsion angles, which identifies it with the discrete Frenet frame of the inscribed orbit polygon. An embedded regular Hahn curve is determined, up to linear reparametrization about $ω_0$, by its trace and the induced contraction. We prove a sharp planarity criterion and a fundamental theorem via an infinite product of rotations and the Jackson--Nörlund integral. For smooth curves, expansions uniform in $q$ show that at $ω_0$ the Hahn curvature and torsion carry the factors $[2]_q/2$ and $[3]_q/3$. These factors, a sampling effect of geometrically decaying steps, disappear under edge-length normalization, but their quotient persists in the limiting ratio of torsion and turning angles of every polygon inscribed in a smooth curve with monotonically converging vertices and edge lengths decaying with ratio~$q$. In uniformly sampled relaxation towards a stable node, the factors can become measurable biases. We characterize generalized Hahn helices by a two-step relation between turning and torsion angles; their Lancret ratio at $ω_0$ is $\pm([2]_q/2)\cot\vartheta$, where $\vartheta$ is the helix angle. Unlike the classical case, a constant ratio of torsion and curvature does not characterize helices: curves with constant curvature and torsion are never generalized Hahn helices, and, near $ω_0$, unit-speed helices with a given ratio are unique up to similarities and linear reparametrization.

entry.title: Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
entry.summary: These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. The lectures centred around algebraic structures arising from twists of supersymmetric quantum field theories, correlation functions of topologically twisted supersymmetric gauge theories, and their mathematical counterparts as intersection-theoretic invariants associated to moduli spaces of instantons, semistable sheaves, or Higgs sheaves on four-manifolds or complex projective surfaces.

entry.title: Generalized Kahler BHE threefolds
entry.summary: We study the notion of generalized Kahler Bismut--Hermitian--Einstein (GKBHE) manifolds, namely generalized Kähler manifolds for which both Bismut Ricci forms vanish, and we develop a theory for such structures on compact threefolds. We organize the analysis according to the horizontal rank, an invariant taking values in $\{0,1,2\}$ that measures the relative position of the canonical foliations associated with the two Hermitian structures. We characterize the case of horizontal rank $0$ (which corresponds to Kähler Ricci flat geometry) and describe the case of horizontal rank $1$, revealing its close interplay with the steady $ν$-soliton equation in Kähler geometry. This description also provides a tool for constructing new compact GKBHE threefolds.

entry.title: On complete Ricci--flat Kähler manifolds
entry.summary: We study complete noncompact Ricci-flat Kähler manifolds. In the case of Euclidean volume growth, we prove that the underlying complex manifold is naturally quasi-projective and that the asymptotic cone is unique. Moreover, we establish no semistability at infinity and prove convergence to the asymptotic cone at a polynomial rate. In the case of sub-Euclidean volume growth, we construct complete Ricci-flat Kähler threefolds with bounded sectional curvature and finite topological type that admit no Kähler compactification.

entry.title: A variational construction for Einstein metrics on connected sums of $S^2\times S^2$
entry.summary: For each positive integer $n$, we give a variational construction of a positive Einstein metric on the connected sum of $n$ copies of $S^2\times S^2$, with coupled toric and dihedral symmetries. More precisely, we obtain these metrics via a min-max construction for the total scalar curvature, which is in some sense dual to the usual max-min formulation of the smooth Yamabe invariant within this symmetry class, with more favorable analytic properties.

entry.title: Finite-Shift Inverse-Concavity and Exterior Noncollapsing for Fully Nonlinear Curvature Flows of Nonconvex Hypersurfaces
entry.summary: We give a finite negative-shift criterion for preserving a prescribed exterior noncollapsing bound under fully nonlinear curvature flows whose hypersurfaces need not be convex. The criterion uses the optimized two-point expression of Andrews and Langford. We verify it by a uniform global two-matrix estimate for the explicit speed \[ F_{\varepsilon}(A)= tr A- \varepsilon\frac{\norm{A^{\circ}}^{2}}{ tr A} \] on the open cone \[ Γ=\{A\in\Sym(n): tr A>0, \norm{A^{\circ}}< tr A\}.\] Here $A^\circ$ denotes the trace-free part of $A$. This cone contains the positive cone and also matrices with a negative eigenvalue, while the displayed speed is concave and non-convex. For an explicit range of parameters depending on the initial exterior bound, the cone and that bound are preserved throughout the smooth embedded existence interval. Together with the known interior estimate for concave speeds, this gives two-sided tangent-ball bounds for this nonlinear family, including closed nonconvex initial hypersurfaces.

entry.title: Rigidity theorems of complete self-shrinkers in the Euclidean space
entry.summary: We classify complete Lagrangian self-shrinking surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant squared norm of the mean curvature vector, without assuming an upper bound for the second fundamental form. Their images are a plane through the origin, the round cylinder $S^1(1)\times \mathbb{R}$, or the Clifford torus $S^1(1)\times S^1(1)$. More generally, a complete self-shrinking surface in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant $|\vec{H}|^2$ is either a plane, a round cylinder, or a complete minimal immersion into $S^3(\sqrt2)$. The proof uses the function $|x|^2-|\vec{H}|^2$, the Bochner formula, and completeness.

entry.title: Fixed geodesics of involutions on $3$-spheres
entry.summary: Let an isometric involution act on a smooth Riemannian $3$-sphere with sectional curvature at least one. We prove that every one-dimensional connected component of its fixed-point set has length at most $2π$, and that the bound is sharp. The proof realizes the fixed circle as the link of a complete totally geodesic surface in a positively curved expanding Ricci soliton and applies Bishop--Gromov comparison to its area growth. The analytic input is an equivariant version of Deruelle's smoothing of positively curved cones. We use Gianniotis--Schulze's equivariant local deformation and explain a marked compactness argument for arbitrary finite isotropy. In particular, the end chart retains the specified group action, rather than only an unspecified conjugate.

entry.title: The sharp Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality and its variants
entry.summary: We introduce and prove a new conformally invariant Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality, and classify all optimizers, which are the Hopf map $π:\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}\to\mathbb{CP}^n$ composed with a symplectic diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and an orientation-preserving conformal transformation of $\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$. The proof uses the sharp curl-Sobolev inequality and a rigidity argument for its equality case. Motivated by the main result, we also introduce the spherical Radu--Tchrakian--Yang functional, and prove the global minimality of the Hopf map for radii in a neighborhood of $((n!)^2/n)^{1/(4n-4)}$, and characterize all minimizers. We also prove local instability for sufficiently small and sufficiently large radii, with explicit lower bounds for the Morse index.

entry.title: Monotonicity and evolution of total isoperimetric profiles under Minkowski regularization
entry.summary: We study the evolution of the total isoperimetric profile of a planar convex body under volume-preserving Minkowski regularization. Several scalar geometric quantities are known to be monotone along this flow; we prove that the total isoperimetric profile is monotone as well, and characterize the equality cases. We also establish an explicit reparametrization law, by which, for nonnegative times, the profile of the regularized body is determined by that of the initial one, and the order of profiles of bodies of equal area is preserved. As consequences, we obtain the uniform convergence of the profile to the one of the ball of equal area; its joint \(\mathrm C^1\) regularity in the volume and the regularization parameter; the fact that it solves a nonlocal quasilinear Hamilton--Jacobi equation; and sharp inequalities for the profile.

entry.title: Scalar curvature integrals on geodesic balls
entry.summary: We study scalar curvature integrals over geodesic balls on complete noncompact manifolds. Under nonnegative Ricci curvature and rotational symmetry, we prove the sharp bound \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}μ_g \le 2n(n-1)ω_n \bigl(1-v^{1/(n-1)}\bigr)r^{n-2}, \] when $p$ is the rotational origin. Here $ω_n$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball and $v=V_{M^n}$ is the asymptotic volume ratio. In dimension three, with the center at a pole, we obtain a sharp bound \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}μ_g\le16πr, \] without any positive volume growth assumption. We also obtain a bound for every asymptotic volume ratio which is sharp for $0\le v\le1/4$. Under nonnegative sectional curvature and $v>0$, we prove the explicit bound at arbitrary centers \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}μ_g\le12π(1-v)v^{-3}r. \] If $0\le1-v\le1/100$, we further obtain \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}μ_g\le\bigl[8π(1-v)+200π(1-v)^2\bigr]r. \] The leading coefficient $8π$ is sharp, and a remainder of quadratic order in $1-v$ is necessary.

entry.title: Examples of absolutely minimal polyhedral chains in maximum norm spaces
entry.summary: We construct explicit area-minimizing polyhedral disks in $\R^n$ with the maximum norm for $n=2,3,4$. Their boundaries are polygonal images of the geodesic circle of length $2π$, obtained from $n$ distance functions. Piecewise constant calibrations show that these disks minimize mass among Ambrosio--Kirchheim metric currents with the same boundary. The example for $n=4$ gives the lower bound $11π^2/20\approx5.42828$ for Gromov's filling area conjecture. For $n>4$, finite linear programs provide further lower bounds.

entry.title: Sharp local scalar-curvature rigidity of spherical caps
entry.summary: Let $B(δ)\subset\mathbb S^n$ be a geodesic ball with the round metric $\bar{g}$ of sectional curvature one, where $n\geq3$ and $0<δ<π/2$. We prove local scalar-curvature rigidity under preservation of the induced boundary metric and a one-sided lower bound for the boundary mean curvature. More precisely, every sufficiently small $C^{2,α}$ perturbation $g$ of $\bar{g}$ satisfying $R(g)\geq n(n-1)$ and $H(g)\geq(n-1)\cotδ$ is round up to a diffeomorphism fixing the boundary pointwise. Inspired by the scalar--vector--tensor decomposition used in the study of Yamabe compactness, we establish positivity of the Brendle--Marques quadratic form in the divergence-free gauge for variations preserving the induced boundary metric and satisfying the joint linearized constraints $D R_{\bar{g}}(h)=D H_{\bar{g}}(h)=0$. The hemisphere counterexamples of Brendle--Marques--Neves show that the radius range is sharp.

entry.title: $L^p$-Liouville properties and realizations of Schrödinger operators on incomplete Riemannian manifolds
entry.summary: The aim of the paper is to highlight and standardize in a self-contained framework the connections between some properties associated with the Laplace-Beltrami operator on possibly incomplete Riemannian manifolds. We present both new and well-known characterizations of the positivity-preserving property, essential self-adjointness, and Liouville-type results for $L^2$-functions, using the latter to establish a clear hierarchy among these properties. Furthermore, we prove the stability of the essential self-adjointness of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on incomplete Riemannian manifolds under the removal of closed (possibly non-compact) subsets from a complete manifold, subject to suitable conditions on their (generalized) Hausdorff measure. With appropriate modifications, this framework is adapted throughout the paper to the general $L^p$-case for $p\in (1,+\infty)$.

entry.title: Scalar--Mean Rigidity for Hyperbolic Balls in Dimensions $2\le n\le 5$
entry.summary: In this paper, we prove the non-spin hyperbolic scalar--mean rigidity theorem in dimensions $2\leq n\leq5$, resolving the corresponding low-dimensional case of a problem of Gromov. The proof combines the Jang deformation with capillary $μ$-bubble dimension reduction. We also establish weighted scalar--mean rigidity for Euclidean ball--torus products in total dimension at most seven and show that its hyperbolic analogue fails.

entry.title: Classification of analytic conformal product structures
entry.summary: We classify real-analytic conformal product structures on compact simply connected manifolds in all dimensions $n\ge 2$. We prove that in dimension $2$ and $3$ no such structure exists, while in every dimension $n\ge 4$ the two parallel distributions arise from a global product splitting.

entry.title: Curvature, second variation and Jacobi fields in elastic diffeology
entry.summary: We develop curvature theory on Blohmann's elastic diffeological spaces. We introduce curvature-tensorial connections, whose curvature factors uniquely through $T_3M$, and show that this property holds on finite-dimensional manifolds and is preserved on mapping spaces. Using a plotwise commutator identity and the elasticity axioms, we establish the classical curvature symmetries for curvature-tensorial Levi-Civita connections. We define sectional curvature and a curvature form on the algebraic exterior square, and demonstrate an obstruction to the usual Ricci trace construction: on $C^\infty(S^1,S^2)$, the relevant curvature endomorphism extends boundedly to the $L^2$ completion but is not trace class. We prove the second variation formula, identify the energy Hessian with the index form, and characterize its null space. Under additional hypotheses, we establish existence and uniqueness of Jacobi fields with prescribed initial data. Finally, non-positive sectional curvature excludes conjugate points, while a negative index direction obstructs length minimization.

entry.title: Mean curvature nonpositivity and rational connectedness
entry.summary: Let $(X,ω)$ be a compact Gauduchon manifold and let $E$ be a holomorphic vector bundle on $X$. We establish equivalent conditions for the existence of a Hermitian metric on $E$ with nonpositive mean curvature. For a non-uniruled compact Kähler manifold $X$ satisfying $μ_{ω_0,\max}(T_X)=0$ for some Gauduchon metric $ω_0$, we show that the corresponding maximal destabilizing subsheaf of $T_X$ splits off holomorphically and is polystable of slope zero with respect to every Gauduchon metric. Its complement, if nonzero, is HN-negative with respect to every such metric. In particular, a compact Kähler manifold is not uniruled if and only if , for every Gauduchon metric $ω$, its tangent bundle admits a Hermitian metric with nonpositive $ω$-mean curvature. We also obtain an uniruledness criterion that includes the case where the maximal slope of $T_X$ is zero, and a Mumford-type characterization of rational connectedness. Under HN-nonnegativity of $T_X$ for one Gauduchon metric, rational connectedness, the vanishing of all holomorphic covariant tensors, and the condition $κ^+(X)=-\infty$ are equivalent.

entry.title: Ramification and Finiteness of Equivariant Minimal Surfaces
entry.summary: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g$, with $g\ \geq \ 2$, and let $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$ be the good locus of $\operatorname{PU}(2,\,1)$ representations with Toledo invariant zero. For $1\ \leq \ b\ \leq\ 2g-3$, we show that representations admitting an equivariant minimal map of total ramification at least $b$, for some marked complex structure, form a countable union of compact null sets of Hausdorff dimension at most $16g-16-2b$. For larger $b$, this locus is empty. Consequently, on a dense $G_δ$ subset of full measure in $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$, every nonconstant equivariant minimal map is an immersion, for every marked complex structure. On the convex cocompact locus, a dense $G_δ$ subset of full measure consists of representations admitting a finite nonempty set of marked equivariant minimal immersions.

entry.title: Isotropy sets of periodic geodesic flows on three dimensional manifolds
entry.summary: A classical theorem of Wadsley states that if all geodesics on a Riemannian manifold M are periodic, then they have a common period, and the geodesic flow induces an S^1-action on the unit tangent bundle. Moreover, a conjecture of Berger asserts that this action is free whenever M is simply connected. In this paper, we investigate the Berger conjecture in dimension three by studying the isotropy set of the S^1-action induced by the geodesic flow. Using Morse theory for the energy functional on the free loop space of M, we establish two results in this direction. First, we show that all isotropy groups of the geodesic flow have odd order. Second, we prove that the geodesic flow either acts freely on the unit tangent bundle $T^1M$ or has at least two singular orbit types. This paper serves as preparation for the subsequent paper The Berger conjecture for three-dimensional manifolds, in which the conjecture is proved in dimension three.

entry.title: Dirichlet eigenvalue asymptotics on conformally compact Einstein manifolds
entry.summary: We study the first Dirichlet eigenvalues of large geodesic balls and fixed-width boundary layers on conformally compact Einstein manifolds of dimension $n+1.$ For large balls, we determine the exponential rate of convergence when the spectral bottom is less than $\frac{n^2}{4},$ i.e. the bottom of the continuous spectrum. When it equals the bottom of the continuous spectrum, the second coefficient has two possible values, according to whether the continued resolvent is regular or has a pole there. We also give examples with negative Yamabe conformal infinity realizing both threshold alternatives and construct metrics with a Ricci lower bound that have other second coefficients. Under nonnegative Yamabe conformal infinity, we also find the exact second coefficient for the nonlinear $p$-Laplacian on large balls. For layers defined by a geodesic boundary defining function, we compute the first correction and show that its sign characterizes nonnegative Yamabe conformal infinity.

entry.title: Calibrations close to $\mathrm{G}_2$-twistor space
entry.summary: We study natural structures of the kind of $\mathrm{G}_2$ existing on the unit tangent sphere bundle $SM \rightarrow M$ of any oriented Riemannian 4-manifold $M$. Based on the Harvey-Morgan classification of degree 3 calibrations on $\mathbb{R}^7$, we identity those which can be found on $SM$. We also study the Laplacian of the Sasaki metric on 3-forms.

entry.title: Harmonic-Einstein maps and critical metrics for eigenvalues of the conformal Laplacian
entry.summary: We prove that Clarke critical metrics for the ratio of the first two eigenvalues of the conformal Laplacian on a closed manifold with positive Yamabe constant correspond to harmonic--Einstein maps into a sphere. We discuss some rigidity consequences, as well as an extension to the higher-order GJMS operators.
